units.source_text: 你还记得吧，我曾跟你说过，社会上并没有天生的坏人，

en.t: You remember, I suppose, that I once told you there are no people in society who are born bad,

units.source_text: 很多好人会在关键时刻突然变成坏人，因此不可不提防。

en.t: and that many good people suddenly become bad at a critical moment, so one must never fail to be on guard.

units.source_text: 当时，你还说我情绪有点激动。

en.t: At the time, you even said that I was a little worked up.

units.source_text: 后来，你又问我，好人在什么情况下会变成坏人。

en.t: Afterward, you asked me again under what circumstances a good person becomes bad.

units.source_text: 当时，我只回答了一个‘钱’字。

en.t: At that time, I answered with only one word: money.

units.source_text: 那时候，你显得不太高兴，我现在还记得你当时的样子。

en.t: Then you seemed rather displeased, and I still remember how you looked at that moment.

units.source_text: 现在，我可以告诉你了，那时我想到的就是这位叔叔。

en.t: Now I can tell you: the person I had in mind then was this uncle.

units.source_text: 我是怀着憎恶，把他作为正常人一见到钱就变成恶人的例子，作为世人皆不可信赖的例子联想起来的。

en.t: With hatred in my heart, I thought of him as an example of an ordinary person who turns bad the moment he sees money, and as an example proving that no one in the world can be trusted.

units.source_text: 我的回答对于要深入探索思想领域的你来说，也许是不能令你满足的，是陈腐不堪的，

en.t: To you, who wanted to explore deeply into the realm of thought, my answer may have been unsatisfying and unbearably stale,

units.source_text: 但是，从我的角度来说，却是活生生的回答。

en.t: but from my point of view, it was a living answer.

units.source_text: 那时，我的确特别激动，我相信，用灼热的舌头叙述平凡的道理，要比用冷静的头脑分析新鲜事物更为生动。

en.t: At that time, I truly was especially excited, and I believe that explaining an ordinary truth with a burning tongue is more vivid than analyzing something new with a cool head.

units.source_text: 因为，人的身体全凭血液推动；

en.t: For the human body is driven entirely by blood;

units.source_text: 因为，语言不仅能使空气产生波动，还能够更强烈地作用于更强之物。

en.t: for language not only makes the air vibrate, but can also act more strongly upon things stronger than air.
